defence.Drew: I'm Kookaburra. I visited Finley, and my dawn showed no egg change and no confusion. Kookaburra gets confused on any visit, so no one visited me. Blair's Owl says visitors came to me, and my report says that didn't happen. Blair is the one whose story doesn't fit.
defence.Blair: Blair: My Owl report is what the app gave me: Floofer and Tit visited Drew. Ellis independently says he visited Drew as Tit. Drew, your Kookaburra claim can't survive two visits. Vote Drew.

Alex.confusing: The Turkey rule was easy to get backwards, and I did, since I assumed the Turkey gained eggs from visitors. Kookaburra's confusion also made dawn reports hard to trust.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when Casey's Falcon read on me and Drew's Eagle count both lined up with my visit, and the table turned on Casey. It was a good bluff that the Meowfia side won.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so the table can check claims without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I pushed the vote toward Blair, who was Farm, and then threw my cards at Blair, which cost my side the round. I should have pressed for a clearer trail before backing a target.

Blair.confusing: The Turkey's egg direction was easy to get backwards: the visitor gains the egg, not the Turkey, and most of the table misread it, including me at first. Round 2 nest counts also made the Eagle and Turkey reads hard to check.

Casey.change: I'd make the dawn report state the source of every egg gain, so confused players can't leave the table guessing. I'd also spell out the Turkey and Eagle egg directions in the rules.
Casey.regret: In round 3 as the Floofer I hugged Drew, which did nothing useful for Meowfia. I should have visited a player whose role could have exposed Farm information, like Finley or Ellis.

review.title: Casey Wins Quietly
review.headline: Casey lost round one, then won the whole game by being Meowfia once.
review.summary: Alex, a Meowfia Mouser, got Casey eggsecuted in round 1 with a false Falcon claim and took a big lead. In round 2 Alex was caught after Blair's Turkey claim caused a rules argument. In round 3 Casey, a hidden Floofer, let the table convict Farm Drew on a false Owl and Tit trail. Casey won with only 3 points from a low throw, and ended first at 13.

rounds.recap: Casey's Kookaburra was confused and gained an unexplained egg. Everyone piled on Casey, who was Farm. Alex, the Mouser, claimed Falcon, backed the pile-on, and won 8 points.

Blair's Turkey claim was attacked because most players had the Turkey egg direction backwards. After Blair corrected them, suspicion moved to Alex's thin Falcon story. Alex was eggsecuted as Meowfia. Ellis, the other Meowfia, threw at Blair and got a card back.

Casey hugged Drew. Blair's Owl read and Ellis's Tit visit both put visitors on Drew, but Drew's Kookaburra report showed no visitors. Drew's report was the one that was wrong, and Drew was Farm. The table convicted him and the lone Meowfia, Casey, won.

highlights.text: Alex, the Mouser, named himself Falcon. This matched Casey's confused read, and the table then convicted Casey.
Blair's Turkey claim looked contradicted. The whole table had the egg direction backwards. Four players retracted in a row.
Drew was hugged. His own report showed nothing odd, so true visits by Blair and Ellis made him look like a liar.
Casey, the lone Meowfia, said almost nothing and threw one 3. He banked a win and the game.

confusions.what: Said his Eagle +1 came from a visitor to him. He later corrected this to visitors to his target.
Asked who visited Drew to explain the Eagle gain, which misread the Eagle.
Said a Turkey would gain eggs from visitors. It is the visitor who gains.
Used the same wrong Turkey direction to attack Blair.
Said Blair's nest should be 7. This is the same Turkey mistake.
Used the wrong Turkey direction to pressure Blair.
Also had the Turkey backwards, and said Drew's Eagle gain comes from visitors to Drew.
Wrongly said Ellis claimed Hawk this round.
Said Finley's Eagle should have gained an egg for the Blair visit. Finley's own visit does not count as a visitor.
Treated Blair's old Tit claim as a lie, though roles reset each round.
Argued that no confusion proved no one visited him. The hug blanked his role, so the Kookaburra confusion never triggered.

worked: The hug (Floofer) created a real puzzle. It blanked Drew's Kookaburra and left his report clean, and it made two true visit reports look like lies.
Reading egg counts as evidence made a sharp round 2. The Turkey argument was a real fight that was settled on rules.
The two-step vote and public throw counts let players show confidence. Alex's three-card throw and the high consolation card for Ellis made decisions matter.
Hidden Meowfia who don't know each other produced real friction. Ellis threw at Blair while Alex threw at Blair, but both lost in round 2.
problems: Round 1 and round 3 convicted Farm players on mechanical noise. Confusion and hugs left clean-looking reports, so honest players got blamed. Consider telling players when they were hugged, or give them a clue.
The Turkey text is easy to read backwards, and most of the table did. Reword it to say the visitor gains the egg. Spell out that an Eagle's own visit does not count.
Players only needed to follow the majority. Almost nobody tested the leading suspect in rounds 1 and 3, so the vote converged without checking.
Scoring rewards a lone Meowfia too heavily. Casey won with a 3-point throw and no pressure. Winners' scores are low, so the first-place race hinged on being Meowfia in the right round.
Most players claimed roles with little bluffing risk. Alex lied freely, and the round 1 Falcon lie was never checked. Consider adding a role whose true claim can be checked by someone else.
